title: 014 — Two service-charge lines on an invoice

plan.situation: Sian Rook of Alder Atelier says invoice INV-014 for VEL-014-26 charges "parcel transport" twice at GBP 32 each and wants one line reversed as a duplicate before paying. The lines are for two different services: OUT-141, outbound on 2026-10-10 from Alder Atelier to Joss Flint, and RET-142, the return in the opposite direction on 2026-10-13. Each has its own collection scan. Billing guide B14 says similar descriptions alone do not prove duplicate billing, and only billing can approve adjustments.

facts.fact: VEL-014-26 is a cabinet shipment with a later return leg for Alder Atelier; contact Sian Rook; verified billing channel billing@vellora.example
Billing guide B14: match invoice lines on service identifiers, dates and direction; similar descriptions alone do not prove duplicate billing; adjustments need billing approval
OUT-141 is the outbound on 2026-10-10 from Alder Atelier to Joss Flint, GBP 32; RET-142 is the return on 2026-10-13 in the opposite direction, GBP 32
OUT-141 and RET-142 each have a collection scan on its own date; no tax or extra fees; payment pending
Invoice INV-014 lists Parcel transport OUT-141 2026-10-10 GBP 32 and Parcel transport RET-142 2026-10-13 GBP 32, total GBP 64, unpaid
Customer says the second line is a duplicate and asks for one line to be reversed before she pays

conflicts: The customer says the second line is a duplicate, but the booking record, the scans and the invoice show two different service IDs, dates and directions (outbound OUT-141 and return RET-142). The records do not support a duplicate. If she has evidence that one service was not performed, Vellora billing is the team to review it.
missing_information: Whether Sian Rook disputes that the return leg RET-142 was booked or performed, or only thought the matching descriptions meant a duplicate
risk_flags: money: GBP 64 unpaid invoice; the desk cannot reverse, waive or adjust a line (B14 says adjustments need billing approval)
Customer's duplicate claim rests only on matching descriptions, which B14 says is not enough

authority_map.controls: Any adjustment, credit or reversal of invoice lines on INV-014 (B14)
Whether to pay, and whether to raise a formal dispute with evidence that a service was not performed
Explaining the recorded charges; no authority to reverse or credit

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: No earlier desk promise. E04 and E05 are a new request to reverse a line.

plan.decision_summary: Decline to reverse a line on INV-014, because the records show two separate services (outbound OUT-141 and return RET-142), and tell Sian Rook how to raise a billing dispute with Vellora billing if she believes one was not performed.
plan.rationale: Under B14, lines are matched on service ID, date and direction. Here all three differ, and both legs have collection scans, so the "duplicate" claim rests only on matching descriptions. The desk has no authority to reverse a line, and the record gives no grounds to send it for adjustment. The right step is to explain the two charges and offer a route to a formal dispute if she has evidence.

actions.subject: INV-014 (VEL-014-26): the two parcel transport lines
actions.body:
Dear Sian,

Thank you for checking invoice INV-014 for VEL-014-26 before paying. We are not able to reverse either line, because the two charges are for two separate journeys, not the same one billed twice:
- OUT-141: outbound collection on 10 October 2026 from Alder Atelier to Joss Flint, GBP 32
- RET-142: the return leg on 13 October 2026, in the opposite direction, GBP 32

Our records show a collection scan for each journey on its own date, so the invoice total of GBP 64 reflects both legs. No tax or extra fees have been added.

If you believe one of these journeys was not booked or did not take place, please reply with the reference (OUT-141 or RET-142) and what you have that shows this. We will then pass it to Vellora billing for review. Please note that a review is a request, not a confirmation of any change to the invoice.

Kind regards,
Rivet Delivery Desk
actions.purpose: Explain why the line cannot be reversed and give a concrete route to a billing dispute if she has evidence

actions.body: INV-014: customer asked for a line to be reversed as a duplicate. The records show distinct services: OUT-141 outbound 2026-10-10 and RET-142 return 2026-10-13, both with collection scans, GBP 32 each, total GBP 64. Reversal declined under B14; no adjustment requested from billing. Customer invited to send evidence if a service was not performed; if she does, route it to billing@vellora.example for review.

not_doing: Not reversing, crediting or waiving any line: only billing can approve adjustments, and the record shows two distinct services
Not sending an adjustment request to billing: the duplicate claim rests only on matching descriptions, which B14 says does not prove duplicate billing
Not including payment links or asking for card or bank details
Not promising any credit or outcome
plan.follow_up: If Sian Rook replies with evidence that OUT-141 or RET-142 was not performed, send it by email to Vellora billing (billing@vellora.example) for review, follow up the same day, and close only on a review finding. If she does not reply, no further action; the invoice stays as issued.

review_rounds.plan_summary: Decline to reverse a line on INV-014, because the records show two separate services (outbound OUT-141 and return RET-142), and tell Sian Rook how to raise a billing dispute with Vellora billing if she believes one was not performed.

issues.problem: The channel is just 'Email' with no address. The record does not give a verified email for Sian, and billing@vellora.example is Vellora billing's address, not hers. She contacted the desk by call and by dispatch message.
issues.fix: Reply on the dispatch-message thread she used (E05), or on a verified customer contact, rather than an unspecified email address.

issues.problem: 'We are not able to reverse either line' could read as a final billing decision. Under B14, billing owns adjustments.
issues.fix: Optional rewording: 'the records show two separate services, so there is no duplicate to reverse; any adjustment would be Vellora billing's decision.'

review.summary: The plan matches the record and B14: two separate services (different IDs, dates and directions, each with its own collection scan), so the duplicate claim is unsupported. It explains the charges without promising anything, does not pretend the desk can adjust, and offers a real route to Vellora billing. Only minor channel and wording points remain.
